t.2.64.1: While Bharata was recounting his dream, those messengers, their mounts exhausted, entered the delightful city of Rājagṛha with its impassable moat.
t.2.64.3: The family priest and all the ministers wish you well. Set out quickly, for there is an urgent matter that must be done by you.
t.2.64.2: Having met them and been honored by the king and the king's son, they clasped the king's feet and spoke these words to Bharata.
t.2.64.4: Here are twenty crores for the king, your maternal uncle, and likewise ten full crores, O son of the king.
t.2.64.5: Having accepted all of that, Bharata, deeply devoted to his kinsfolk and friends, honoured the messengers with whatever they desired and then spoke to them.
t.2.64.7: And is Kausalyā, the noble mother of the wise Rāma, devoted to dharma, knowing dharma and beholding dharma, also free from illness?
t.2.64.6: I hope the king, my father Daśaratha, is in good health? And I hope Rāma and the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa are free from illness?
t.2.64.8: Is Sumitrā, the knower of dharma, who is the mother of Lakṣmaṇa and of the heroic Śatrughna, the middle queen, also in good health?
t.2.64.9: Kaikeyī, my mother, ever self-seeking, fierce, wrathful, and proud of her own wisdom, is she in good health, and what did she say?
t.2.64.10: Thus addressed by the great-souled Bharata, the messengers then spoke these courteous words to Bharata: "O tiger among men, those whose welfare you desire are well."
t.2.64.12: Having spoken thus to those messengers, Bharata, the son of the king, urged on by the messengers, addressed these words to his maternal grandfather.
t.2.64.11: Thus addressed, Bharata in turn spoke to those messengers: “I take leave of the great king, O messengers; they are urging me to make haste.”
t.2.64.13: O king, urged by the messengers, I shall go to my father's presence. I will come back again whenever you think of me.
t.2.64.14: Thus addressed by Bharata, the king, his maternal grandfather, then smelled the head of that Rāghava and spoke these auspicious words to him.
t.2.64.15: Go, dear son, I give you leave; in you Kaikeyī is blessed with a worthy son. Convey my wishes for their welfare to your mother and your father, O scorcher of foes.
t.2.64.16: Ask after the well-being of the family priest and of those other excellent twice-born, and, dear one, of those two great archers, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
t.2.64.17: Having honored him, the Kaikeya gave wealth to Bharata: the finest elephants, colorful blankets, and deerskins.
t.2.64.18: Having honored the son of Kaikeyī, the king of Kekaya bestowed wealth upon him: two thousand niṣkas of gold and sixteen hundred horses.
t.2.64.19: Likewise Aśvapati swiftly gave to Bharata ministers as followers, men who were agreeable, trustworthy and endowed with good qualities.
t.2.64.20: His maternal uncle gave him wealth: elephants of the Airāvata and Aindraśira breeds, lovely to behold, and swift, well-yoked asses.
t.2.64.22: Having taken leave of his maternal grandfather and of his maternal uncle Yudhājit, Bharata mounted his chariot and departed, accompanied by Śatrughna.
t.2.64.21: He also gave as a gift dogs raised within the inner palace, huge of body, armed with fangs, and endowed with the valor and strength of tigers.
t.2.64.23: Having yoked more than a hundred round-wheeled carts to camels, oxen, horses and donkeys, the servants followed behind the chariot as Bharata went on his way.
t.2.64.24: Guarded by an army, the great-souled Bharata, who had no enemies, took Śatrughna with him and set out from the house together with his grandfather's ministers, who were like his own self, as a Siddha departs from the world of Indra.
